history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 603 ('Balaji Temple Seminary Hills', id 'balaji-temple-seminary-hills-nagpur'): this CSV row 'Shri Balaji Shri Karthikeya Temple, Nagpur' refers to the very same temple - the Sri Balaji and Sri Kartikeya Temple atop Seminary Hills, Nagpur, run by the same Motibagh Shri Skanda Samaj trust. A separate file is written for this seq with a distinct id; the two rows should be merged or deduplicated in the master dataset. The temple is a three-tier structure with a 60-feet Rajagopuram blending South Indian (Rajagopuram) and North Indian (mandapam) orders, enshrining Lord Balaji (6-ft idol, lower sanctum) and Lord Kartikeya with Valli and Deivanai (3-ft idol, upper sanctum), plus shrines of Shiva, Ganapathy, Hanuman, Durga, Shithala Matha, Sarparaja, Maha Sastha and the Navagrahas. The complex includes flower and Tulsi gardens, a community hall, library, priest quarters and a Vedic Pathshala, and doubles as a cultural centre for Nagpur's South Indian community. No documented founding date found in any source (verify).

name: Shri Balaji Shri Karthikeya Temple
town_description: Nagpur is the winter capital and second capital of Maharashtra, the largest city of the Vidarbha region and a major commercial and transport hub, famous for its oranges (the 'Orange City'). It is a premier rail junction linking all four metropolitan cities of India and is served by the Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport. The city has a sizeable South Indian population; its most revered South Indian temple stands atop the scenic Seminary Hills about 6 km north-west of the city centre.
tradition: Hinduism (Vaishnavism and Shaivism - unique Vishnu-Shiva temple)

travel.airport: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport, Nagpur; approx. 12-15 km from Seminary Hills (verify).

travel.road: About 6 km north-west of Nagpur city centre atop Seminary Hills, on Seminary Hills Road; city buses, taxis and auto-rickshaws available.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February for pleasant weather. Brahmotsavam and Skanda Shashti are the grandest times but draw heavy crowds; weekday mornings are best for peaceful darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 6:00 AM to 11:00 AM; evening 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM (verify - one listing shows mornings from 7:00 AM; Fri-Sun morning hours extend to 12:00 noon per another listing). Modest dress expected; photography generally restricted inside the main shrine.
